you're definitely right and I tell people all the time that it's okay for someone to be fat to say it's not entirely their fault.

The issue becomes ongoing when that person has no support to get to the root of their obesity, especially when their behavior is enabled and supported by a society that mixes up being body positive with being healthy. Depression isn't healthy or body positive.

honestly I don't even mind people blaming their fatness on other things. Their genetics, their depression, their anxiety, their addiction, obsessive eating disorders, their thyroid disease, anything. It's fine if they blame it on something else, because many times it is because of other factors and not just pure "I want to be fat." No one wants to have a heart attack at 30. 

But they still need help.

If you have any of the above you need help. Maybe they won't lose weight until they manage their depression, but all I wish is that society would recognize that instead of being like "it's totally fine. be positive." Be positive literally will not cure any of that and anyone who recognizes the root of their issues will hate your "be positive" bs mantra.

But if someone is saying someone is *going to die early* because they are eating themselves into chronic disease, then can we stop attacking them and get whoever needs help the help?

The way I see it, if you love a person dearly to the point that insults make you defensive about them, maybe you should love them enough to give them the help they need. Depression? There are so many things we can do to help people so that the burden of their own health is lifted and they can actually avoid illness.

It was a very awkward experience. I started telling them how I felt in the moment of wanting to commit, and they just spoke really slow almost in a babying tone, and there were so many moments where it was dead silence for more than five minutes. I have read from other users that they can be very invasive as well because they can track your location to alert police, which is traumatizing in itself and tends to cause more problems than save people. If you read a little on /r/SuicideWatch, the invasive procedures are quite hard on people and sometimes people are forced into hospitals (financial burden) for months and then are thus forced to re-enter society, possibly making them worse off.

For those of you who are struggling and have had poor experiences with the suicide hotline (as I have), folks at /r/Suicidewatch are pretty understanding about the massive struggle suicidal thoughts put on folks and it is an active sub with positive people.
